senses.sense_definition: A person who falsely claims to have certain skills, qualities, knowledge, or beliefs; an imposter or charlatan.

examples.text: The self-proclaimed financial guru turned out to be nothing more than a cunning <w>pretender</w>.
Critics quickly dismissed the new author as a <w>pretender</w> trying to imitate classic literature.

senses.sense_definition: A claimant to a throne, crown, or royal title, especially one whose claim is contested or considered illegitimate.

examples.text: The exiled prince was seen by many as a dangerous <w>pretender</w> to the crown.
History remembers him as a bold <w>pretender</w> who failed to overthrow the king.

senses.sense_definition: A person who aspires to, seeks, or lays claim to a position, title, or honor.

examples.text: Several young athletes emerged as serious <w>pretenders</w> for the championship title this season.
The committee reviewed the credentials of every <w>pretender</w> before making a final selection.

senses.sense_definition: A person who seeks the affections or hand in marriage of someone; a suitor.

examples.text: Her father refused to grant an audience to any wealthy <w>pretender</w> seeking her hand.
She rejected every <w>pretender</w> who came courting her during the long summer.

traits.comment: Used in historical or literary contexts.

senses.sense_definition: A person who intends, purposes, or aims to do something.

examples.text: In the archaic lexicon, the word described a <w>pretender</w> who merely formed an intention.
He was an earnest <w>pretender</w> who sought reform before circumstances forced him to withdraw.

senses.sense_definition: To submit or invite a formal bid or contract in advance of the main procurement process.

examples.text: The government decided to <w>pretender</w> critical equipment contracts to save time later.
Officials met early to <w>pretender</w> key materials before launching the construction phase.
